attribution.note: Marcus asserts the ROI and reliability problems in his own voice; these are separate from the quoted analogy.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the majority qualifier and ongoing reliability assertion. The surrounding speculative analogy does not make these factual premises a forecast.

contract.note: Enterprise trial deployments and demonstrated financial returns are ordinary contextual readings. The latest completed quarter is a reasonable recent observation window, although supplied by the evaluator rather than Marcus.

evidence.note: Relevant background from 2025, outside the target period. Its sample and measurable P&L impact metric do not establish representative 2026 pilot ROI.
The survey covers the target period but counts organizations by maturity and enterprise value, not individual pilots by financial ROI.
Considered as counterevidence: reported value exceeding cost concerns respondents' overall AI activity. It cannot establish the proportion of profitable generative-AI pilots.
The March research reports persistent hallucination and grounding failures alongside mitigation results. It supports the reliability component only; experiment dates are unspecified.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports continuing reliability problems but supplies no representative target-period pilot counts with comparable financial costs and returns. Neither the older pilot report nor organization-level surveys settle the majority assertion. Partial support with an unsettled component does not establish a mixed outcome.
